sophia_support: Hey — escalating from ticket #4521. Acme reported intermittent tail latency spikes on our text-gen endpoint between 2026-03-10T15:20Z and 15:50Z. They attached three request ids: req_645f3a, req_645f3b, req_645f3c. p95 usually ~1.8s but they saw spikes to ~9s and p99 ~12s. They say they use model gptx-6b-q4 with streaming enabled.

acme_sre: We saw the same. Repro is non-deterministic but correlates with concurrency bursts (8-12 concurrent). Minimal curl they used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model":"gptx-6b-q4","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":150,"stream":true}'
```
Logs from client side (truncated):
```
2026-03-10T15:21:02.134Z request=req_645f3a duration=920ms status=200
2026-03-10T15:22:11.502Z request=req_645f3b duration=9100ms status=200
2026-03-10T15:22:12.017Z request=req_645f3c duration=11800ms status=200
```

raj_infra: Thanks — can you collect our standard debug bundle for those request ids and upload? If customer can't share API key, request ids + full raw responses are fine. To collect internally run:```bash
/opt/redwood/bin/collect_debug --req req_645f3a,req_645f3b,req_645f3c --out=acme-03010.tgz
```
Or ask them to hit our public endpoint:```bash
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <support-token>\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/bundle?request_ids=req_645f3a,req_645f3b\" -o acme-03010.tgz
```
Also include the exact reproduction parameters: concurrency, per-request token counts, and whether streaming/chunked responses were used.

mike_oncall: I've pulled infra metrics for the window — host gpu-12 shows CPU/GPU scheduling spikes and KV cache miss rate increased ~x3. P95 latency jump aligns with bursts from the same tenant hitting a single serving shard. If we can't reproduce in replay, we'll instrument the runtime and capture per-request kernel timings. Can the customer try the same curl with streaming disabled to see if that changes behavior? :eyes:

acme_sre: Uploading bundle now to a secure bucket (no keys included): https://s3.redwood-acme/test-bundles/acme-03010.tgz . We can't rotate keys mid-incident; included raw responses and a minimal prompt set (10 prompts). Token stats: input tokens ~320, avg output tokens ~1,300. Observed p99 ~12s at concurrency=8 during our test.

raj_infra: Got the bundle, starting a deterministic replay against the same model flavor and quantization profile. Repro plan: 1) single-thread replay of those request ids 2) concurrency sweep (1,4,8,12) with same prompt set and token caps 3) measure per-token time and KV cache hit/miss. If we hit it, we'll collect perf traces. If you can, also paste the exact curl you used for concurrency tests (http version, connection reuse flags).

acme_sre: Example concurrency curl we used (we used http2 and chunked streaming):```bash
# concurrency runner (example)
for i in $(seq 1 8); do 
  curl -k --http2 -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-6b-q4","input":"<prompt X>","max_tokens":1300,"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
Also note we use long outputs (1k+ tokens) so backend tokenization/kv-cache behavior matters.

sophia_support: Thanks all — I'm adding this thread to the ticket and marking as escalated to eng-runtime. Action items for customer: upload debug bundle (done), confirm concurrency test command (done), provide any client-side network logs. Action items for infra: run replay + collect perf traces if repro. ETA 24-48h. Closing loop once we have repro pack and a short write-up. :raised_hands:
